We joined Superintendent Anthony Dixon of BCSD and Berkeley County Chamber of Commerce CEO Elaine Morgan to recognize the Teachers of the Year in each school across Berkeley County.

Our office wrote individual letters to congratulate each teacher on their awards. Their hard work and dedication are evident.

To every teacher recognized: the Lowcountry is better because of you. Thank you for everything you do for our children.

South Carolina STRONG.

It's 2am and I just walked off the floor after passing three of my amendments to the Farm Bill.

First, we codified President Trump's executive order for the USDA Office of Seafood and second, we unlocked USDA agricultural programs for our commercial fishermen. South Carolina’s shrimping and fishing economy is the backbone of our coastal heritage, and it is time our farmers of the sea received the same backing as those on land. Anthony Fauci looked Congress in the eye and lied under oath about funding research tied to a pandemic killing millions of people worldwide, which he then used as justification to shut down our country.

A four-year college degree is not in the cards for everyone.

America needs skilled workers. Electricians. Welders. Plumbers. HVAC technicians. The people who keep this country running every single day.

Trade schools, apprenticeships, and alternative workforce programs are not a lesser path. They are a direct path to a good-paying career.

We fully support every South Carolinian choosing a trade, an apprenticeship, or a non-traditional path into the workforce. Education is not one size fits all

This funding helps finance affordable housing projects and ensures taxpayer-supported incentives are driving responsible, long-term solutions. It should not be out of reach for Americans to find an affordable place to live, especially in the Lowcountry as it continues to grow.

My father served three tours of combat, two in Vietnam, one in the Dominican Republic, and was the most decorated combat veteran The Citadel has ever produced. 

Stolen valor is not a gray area. When a Member of Congress fabricates the stories of dead and injured soldiers for personal gain, the word "disgrace" is too polite.

To Secretary Hegseth and the Department of War: your hard work, your innovation and your legacy is worthy of our nation's military and of men like my father.

Washington has ignored the hardworking men and women who keep South Carolina's coastal economy alive for far too long.

We filed an amendment to the Farm Bill opening up USDA's Local Agriculture Market Program (LAMP) grants to commercial fishing and fish processing businesses, allowing wild-caught American seafood to qualify as an eligible agricultural commodity for domestic seafood marketing activities.

Our office was hosted by the Town of Port Royal, along with Rebecca Cavalier, a marine biologist with the South Carolina Department of Natural Resources, to talk about the best ways to responsibly interact with wildlife in our area.

The local community joined to learn about alligators and the best practices to use when you encounter one. We gained valuable insight into safety practices, habitat conservation, and what we can do to preserve the wildlife of the Lowcountry.
